India’s building automation market is projected to expand from $4.32 billion in 2025 to $12.56 billion by 2030, registering a CAGR of 23.8% industry officials said quoting a MarketsandMarkets report.
“This momentum is reflected in the CII–Cushman & Wakefield report, which projects IoT-enabled automation across organised commercial office built-up area to increase from 25% to 45% by FY2030, alongside integrated building automation and management systems rising from 8% to 23%” said Sakhee Chandrayan, Founder & President, Integrated Building Automation Community (INBAC).
“With digital optimisation offering potential energy savings of 5–40%, as highlighted by the International Energy Agency (IEA), future investments will increasingly prioritise AI-driven analytics, digital twins, predictive maintenance, cybersecurity and secure interoperability,” she said while speaking at ORGATEC India 2026, organised by Koelnmesse Pvt Ltd in Mumbai.
India’s transition from a global back-office destination to a hub for innovation and value creation, accelerated by the rise of Global Capability Centres (GCCs), is reshaping the corporate workplace industry according to Ankur Yagnik, Managing Partner, The Design Construct.
“With the Indian economy expected to grow at 7–8% over the next five years, we anticipate industry growth of at least 15–16%. Indian workplace design standards and indigenous sensibilities are increasingly finding acceptance across global corporations,” he said.
The shift towards ‘work from anywhere’ is redefining offices as destinations for collaboration, cultural integration and team building. AI is driving an invisible transformation, enhancing spatial efficiency without significant physical infrastructure changes. Rising corporate budgets and evolving expectations have also elevated superior acoustics and visual comfort from discretionary features to essential workplace standards, he added.
Highlighting the push toward human-centric engineering at workspaces Karan Sachdev, Managing Director, KOKUYO Workplace India,
said, “At a time when much of the industry continues to evolve around established approaches to product design and development, we are pushing the boundaries further by placing advanced technology, research, and engineering at the heart of innovation.”
Fundamentally the company is rethinking how products function and respond to human needs, Mr Sachdev remarked.
Speaking at ORGATEC India 2026, Milind Dixit, Managing Director, India & SAARC, Koelnmesse Pvt Ltd. said, “India’s commercial real estate sector is witnessing sustained growth, with investments rising 15% year-on-year during the first nine months of 2026. This presents considerable opportunities for the workplace industry.”
According to Tanmay Khare, Vice President & Group Head – Administration, Bajaj Finserv the facility management sector would grow in line with the rapidly growing workspace segment.
“India’s facility management industry, spanning over 100 services, is growing at 20–30% year-on-year and is poised to become one of the country’s largest employment generators,” he said.
He added that corporate real estate demand was moving beyond metros towards emerging business hubs, driven by infrastructure accessibility and operational efficiencies.
As per latest trend corporates are giving distinct look and feel to their workspaces and weaving in branding with the help of specialists.
“As hybrid work reshapes office routines, companies are asking more of their workplaces. They want spaces that give people a reason to come together, support different ways of working and adapt as teams evolve” said Nalin Gagrani, CEO & Managing Director, Blue Pebble Ltd.
“We bring spatial branding, design and build, and immersive experiences together to meet those needs. We use art, storytelling and craftsmanship to make an organisation’s culture tangible, while modular design and thoughtful material choices help spaces stay relevant over time,” he stated.
“We are also exploring how AI can broaden early design exploration and how 3D printing can bring more intricate, site-specific artworks into the workplace. For us, the value of these tools is measured in what they make possible for the people who use the space every day,” he added.
